record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: ReLU tropical functions as quiver theories
record.original_question: Given the connection between tropical geometry through amoebae and quiver gauge theories, can the tropical functions realized by ReLU neural networks be reformulated as quiver gauge theories?

evidence.quote: Question 32. Can the tropical functions describing ReLU NNs be redescribed as quiver gauge theories?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A ReLU neural network defines a continuous piecewise-linear function f: R^n → R^m by alternating affine maps with the activation ReLU(x) = max(x, 0). Every such function can equivalently be written as a difference of two tropical (max-plus) polynomials, i.e. f = P ⊖ Q where P(x) = max_{i}(⟨a_i, x⟩ + b_i) and Q(x) = max_{j}(⟨c_j, x⟩ + d_j) with integer (or rational) slope vectors a_i, c_j and real constants b_i, d_j; equivalently f is a tropical rational function on R^n. On the other hand, to a quiver gauge theory (a finite directed multigraph Q with a dimension vector and a choice of superpotential / matter content) one can associate, via mirror symmetry and the amoeba/tropicalization of its mirror Newton polynomial, a tropical (piecewise-linear) function on a real vector space describing, for example, the tropical limit of its partition function or the support of its amoeba.

Problem. Construct a procedure that, given an arbitrary tropical function f: R^n → R^m arising from a ReLU neural network (specified by its layer-wise weights and biases, equivalently by its representation as a tropical rational map with integer slopes), produces a quiver gauge theory whose associated tropical/amoeba function coincides with f. More precisely: characterize the class of tropical functions realizable as ReLU networks that admit such a quiver-gauge-theoretic realization, give an explicit dictionary translating the network data (weights, biases, depth, width) into quiver data (nodes, arrows, dimension vector, superpotential), and determine whether every ReLU tropical function can be so realized, or otherwise identify the obstructions.
artifact.category_tag: Tropical geometry and quiver gauge theories
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions in quiver gauge theory (2021). No subsequent work appears to provide a quiver-gauge-theoretic reformulation of generic ReLU tropical functions; related literature on tropical geometry of neural networks (Zhang–Naitzat–Lim and follow-ups) and on amoebae of quiver theories has not bridged the two frameworks in the manner asked.
